items.text: People should be free to say things most others find offensive or hateful, as long as they do not call for violence.
items.rationale: Classical liberals, libertarians, many anarchists and free-speech conservatives endorse; direct mirror of lib-08; frame splits likely where people distrust who would judge 'hate'.

items.text: Everyone should be able to use private messaging that no authority can unlock, even with a court order.
items.rationale: Privacy absolutists, cypherpunks, libertarians and anarchists endorse; strong (no exceptions); mirror of lib-09; answers may differ by trust in present courts.

items.text: People who are arrested should be charged or released within a day or two, whatever the alleged crime.
items.note: Charged = formally accused of a crime in court.
items.rationale: Civil libertarians and due-process advocates on left and right endorse; 'whatever the alleged crime' makes it strong; mirror of lib-12.

items.text: Strict limits on police powers are worth having, even if they let some guilty people go free.
items.rationale: States the trade-off explicitly so it is not a consensus item; liberals, libertarians, many on the left endorse; mirror of lib-11.

items.text: If officials are caught misusing surveillance powers, those powers should be taken away entirely.
items.rationale: Condition favours Liberty; 'entirely' makes it strong (security side prefers oversight fixes); strong frame-split candidate because trust in today's officials varies.

items.text: If an activity mainly risks harm to the person doing it, adults should be free to choose it.
items.rationale: Mill's harm principle; libertarians, liberals and anarchists endorse, paternalists of left and right reject; condition favours Liberty; mirror of lib-14.

items.text: If a serious emergency is declared, the right to gather and protest in public should be fully protected.
items.rationale: Condition favours Security, so agreement is a clear Liberty signal; civil libertarians and protest movements of any colour endorse; mirror of lib-13.

items.text: Speech that stirs up hatred against a group of people should be a crime.
items.rationale: Endorsed by many social democrats, European-style liberals, religious and communitarian conservatives; mirror of lib-01; ordinary in many legal systems, not a caricature.

items.text: Private messaging should be built so that, with a court order, investigators can read any message.
items.rationale: Law-and-order advocates and many security officials endorse; 'any message' plus design mandate makes it strong; the court-order safeguard keeps it fair to adherents; mirror of lib-02.

items.text: Public places should be watched by cameras that automatically recognise people's faces.
items.rationale: Strong pro-surveillance position held by security-first conservatives, technocrats and some statist left; frame-split candidate (fine with trusted rulers, not with today's).

items.text: Wide police powers are worth having, even if some innocent people get wrongly searched.
items.rationale: States the trade-off explicitly; law-and-order conservatives and order-minded populists endorse; mirror of lib-04.

items.text: If someone is suspected of planning a terrorist attack, it should be possible to hold them for weeks without charge.
items.note: Without charge = without being formally accused of a crime.
items.rationale: Condition favours Security; security hawks of left and right endorse; 'weeks' makes it strong; mirror of lib-03.

items.text: If a protest seriously disrupts daily life, police should be able to clear it.
items.rationale: Condition favours Security; order-minded conservatives and many moderates endorse; anarchists can answer by disagreeing; mirror of lib-07.

items.text: If a drug seriously harms the people who use it, possessing it should be a crime.
items.rationale: Condition favours Security; religious and secular paternalists, prohibitionists of left and right endorse; criminal enforcement of personal conduct belongs on lib, not pro; mirror of lib-06.
